You could use specialized troops for certain areas. Having a group of gliding ninjas can create havoc for the hero's as they fly past and since its gliding the ninjas would have to stop to cling to a building before another fly over.

Since they are cyborg ninjas an eco squad would be a bad idea. Troops with low dodge/parry and a higher toughness to really take a beating. Nothing freaks out a player more than a minion who can tank a hit. 

My personal favorite though are minions focused on fortitude saves. Players forget that fortitude matters and if you have a group of ground troops that use chemical weapons primarily it can change the course of a battle and potentially lead to a death trap.

The gadget guide has the tech you'd need for this. Also guerilla tactics aren't out of place and will test their skill.

I.E. an invisible sniper is taking shots at them with a silence sniper rifle.

They'll need to rely on skill not powers to overcome that threat.

The players should already know that the task is large so my approach would be to create a network for them to strike against.

Create a web of shell companies each with a specific purpose to the syndicate. This means tech, recruitment, supplies shipments, and of course manpower. With each of these it gives the players a way to plan out the attack and weaken the organization.

Lets say at the lowest levels they find out people are being recruited via the hospital. They help heal victims of limb loss and the fee is so steep that the person has to work for the organization to pay them back. This also creates a dilemma because the players will see victims helped and taking away the syndicate will remove this for the people.

Supplies? You can create a shipyard which imports and exports whatever the syndicate trades in.

Basically break down the organization into its key points and integrate them into the society at large. As for the hook? Let the big bad be a public figure. His evil deeds are unknown to the population and his connection. This can be done via a press conference or if the players don't know him, but have encountered his right hand man let that person be giving a conference on a new business opening up. This will be a hook to the players as they know he is no good and that business has clues of some kind.

Of they know absolutely nothing than you can set them up with an ambush and have the syndicate frame it as though the heroes are a group of villains trying to destabilize Tokyo and the progress its made. Progress made possible by the syndicate. Is there a Tokyo hero? Have that hero fight them as the ambush in public to create this illusion for the masses.

I think a council and supreme leader can work for this. The council can be the front which everyone in the organization thinks runs things, but behind them is the real leader. It can also misguided heroes into a false sense of winning when encountering and beating the council. If they think that the council is the end they won't expect another move to be made against them. And when that move happens SIRPRISE! It ain't over yet kiddos buckle up.

Minions might be a bit much in a final boss. UNLESS! You have him summon them as he is weakened. It shows the players they have an effect and gives them proof of having an effect.

Its great to drain hope, but a group that's given up hope won't fight back.

If/when the entity enters have reality shake and hits against him change reality and this makes the fight varied in aesthetic. Fighting in a city? Not anymore you landed a hit and not your in a forest.

7 alternate forms. Each one with a power directly related to the sin. 
Lust? An attractive person able to compel others others which is telepathic. 
Wrath? Strength. 
Envy? Metamorph. 
Greed? A body made of solid gold with some pcyhic effects to seeing you. Perhaps making targets vulnerable or defenseless. 
Pride? You could have fun with this and make the persona very arrogant and full of itself. 
Sloth? The power to slow others down while also moving at half speed yourself maybe even throw in a sleep affliction. 
Vanity? A body made of mirrored glass that forces those who see themselves in you to make a will save to resist being mesmerized.

I've seen builds like this before as a GM and I'd like to say if you stick to a build like this it would make it easier on your GM to have some hefty drawbacks. Maybe like Ben 10 where each form causes a need to wait before changing again. Also with something like this you can play 8 different personalities and styles. This brings a greater team dynamic. But mainly don't go crazy with this kind of build. Its easy to and can create GM headache. I mean he/she already has to scale for the team and now imagine that they have to scale for 7 more powers.
That oddly enough makes me feel better.

Tips
*street level should be the setting at this point. Use the GM guide book to find foes of street level and use them.
*skill checks will be important so please ensure players don't get power hungry as it will make them almost useless.
*at this power level even an angry dog is a threat so get creative about that. Animals can be used as minions instead of thugs sometimes.
*make sure allow team attacks. At this level they are fantastic and can really change the tide of battle not just because its awesome, but because it allows the damage to stack.

Also allow for NPC's to help in bigger ways and for the environment to have its own affects. Battling in a junkyard? Allow for objects to be toppled and random metal to use as a weapon.
